summary: Merged cost-center tag attrition causing elevated tariff on finalized invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected surcharge line on their finalized February invoice after a recent cost-center consolidation. The surcharge corresponds to ~18% more than the console estimate and appears as a higher tariff applied to multiple line items that previously carried a negotiated discount.

Impact:
- Customer (Calyx AI, enterprise) received a finalized invoice with an extra $12,800 charge.
- Potential contract / billing dispute for February invoice.
- Customer cannot pay until clarification due to internal chargeback process.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1) billing pipeline and postback reconciler.
- Customer uses multiple API keys across subteams; they recently merged cost-center tags in their org.

Timeline (key events):
- 2026-02-25: Calyx merges internal cost-center tag namespace into single tag via Console UI.
- 2026-03-01 02:00 UTC: Billing run for February finalization.
- 2026-03-02: Calyx submits support ticket reporting invoice variance.
- 2026-03-10: Support triage and escalation to billing engineering.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Locate postbacks for Calyx API keys between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28.
2) Run reconciliation script that groups by "cost_center_tag" and "rate_plan_id".
3) Compare grouping results before and after tag normalization window (pre-merge vs post-merge).

Observed behaviour:
- During the final billing run, tag normalization logic collapsed legacy aliases into a single canonical tag but did not map legacy negotiated-rate IDs. As a result, multiple postbacks that should have carried negotiated_rate_id=NR-42 were attributed to the canonical tag with default_rate_id=STD-1. The reconciliation then billed at the default tariff for those grouped line items.
logs: SQL: SELECT api_key, original_tag, canonical_tag, negotiated_rate_id, rate_id FROM postback_ledger WHERE customer_id='calyx' AND date >= '2026-02-01' AND date <= '2026-02-28' LIMIT 50;
Sample ledger row BEFORE normalization: {api_key: 'ak-xxxx', original_tag: 'cc-west-research', canonical_tag: NULL, negotiated_rate_id: 'NR-42', rate_id: 'NR-42'}
Sample ledger row AFTER normalization: {api_key: 'ak-xxxx', original_tag: 'cc-west-research', canonical_tag: 'cc-calyx-primary', negotiated_rate_id: NULL, rate_id: 'STD-1'}
Billing run log: billing-run-2026-03-01.log shows grouping by canonical_tag with 1,482 affected postbacks for customer_id=calyx
Console event: User 'jessica@calyx.ai' performed tag-merge action at 2026-02-25T18:34:11Z (Console audit id A-9988)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: tag merge removed legacy alias mapping between original_tag -> negotiated_rate_id. Billing grouping used canonical_tag only and then applied rate lookup which defaults when negotiated_rate_id is missing.
Confirmed via SQL that ~1,482 postbacks lost negotiated_rate_id during normalization. Sum(delta) shows $12,805.32 higher billed amount compared to pre-normalization grouping.

Found related change: PR 5432 updated tag-normalizer to drop deprecated 'legacy_rate_alias' column when canonicalizing tags. The PR did not include a migration to preserve negotiated_rate_id mappings (see github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5432).

Repro on staging: replayed postbacks with original_tag preserved -> grouping applied NR-42 and invoice totals matched console estimate. Replayed with normalized canonical_tag -> default rate applied and totals matched customer's finalized invoice.
comments: 2026-03-02 — calyx-support@calyx.ai: 'We consolidated cost centers last week and now our February invoice is 18% higher. Please advise. We need an explanation and provisional credit to clear internal PO hold.'

2026-03-10 — Aisha Kapoor (Support): 'Thanks for filing — triaging to billing eng. I've escalated to Marcus Li and created this ticket for tracking. We will request provisional credit while we investigate.'

2026-03-11 — Marcus Li (Billing Eng): 'I ran a reconciliation diff and verified the rate_id attrition. Holding off on final remediation until we confirm safe retroactive application of negotiated rates. Filed INT-9090 for billing-service fix and migration.'
2026-03-11 — Finance (Ticket): 'Calyx requested provisional credit to unblock payment. Recommend issuing provisional credit equal to delta pending root cause fix.'
2026-03-12 — Support (Aisha): 'Applied provisional credit of $12,806 on 2026-03-12 (credit id CR-90821). Customer notified and Finance approved. See resolution notes.'
resolution: Provisional credit applied and customer refunded the delta to clear their PO hold. Billing engineering scheduled a migration to preserve negotiated_rate_id mappings during tag normalization (INT-9090). Patch to billing-run will be deployed as a hotfix in the March 15 window, with a retroactive re-run option to apply negotiated rates to February postbacks if safe. Finance will monitor and issue any final adjustments once migration completes.
